newsitem.title: POLAND: Japanese firms mull purchase of Polish components.
newsitem.headline: Japanese firms mull purchase of Polish components.

text.p: Japanese manufacturers active in Western Europe are mulling buying components in Central and Eastern Europe, the Warsaw head of the governmental Japan External Trade Organisation (JETRO) said on Monday.

Ichiro Arima told a news conference that a Polish-Japanese investment seminar will take place from March 3 to March 5 next year in which the purchase of Polish parts and Japanese investment will be discussed.
"The main purpose of today's conference is to announce that such a meeting will take place," Arima said.
He said 49 Japanese industrial firms operating in Western Europe had expressed interest in investing in Poland.

Japanese companies seek to buy from Polish suppliers parts in the machine, electronics, construction, chemical, electrotechnical, steel, car, telecomunications and other industries, JETRO said in a statement.

Last month Poland's Panstwowa Agencja Inwestycji Zagranicznych (PAIZ) foreign investment agency said that by the end of the first quarter this year Japanese investment in Poland was at $33 million, only about 0.4 percent of all foreign investment in Poland.
The number put Japan in 22nd place among foreign investors in the country.
PAIZ said investors from Far Eastern countries were likely to start flocking to Poland in the next few years after a period dominated by companies from the United States and the European Union.
Jetro's Arima said a main reason for low activity of Japanese industry in Poland was a low understanding of Polish market conditions and Japanese investors' prejudices about the country.
